# Replicate records between tools for utilities

**Pattern:** Two-System Sync · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers utilities work end to end across Google Sheets, HubSpot and Telegram.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Load Previous Snapshot
3. Fetch Changes (Google Sheets)
4. Normalize Records
5. Upsert into Google Sheets
6. Advance Watermark
7. Persist Watermark (HubSpot)
8. Guard Non-Empty type
9. Tag Pipeline Metadata
10. Save Execution Metadata
11. Cap Batch Volume
12. Sort Jobs Newest First
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
15. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing utilities work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Load Previous Snapshot → Fetch Changes (Google Sheets) → Normalize Records → Upsert into Google Sheets → Advance Watermark → Persist Watermark (HubSpot) → Guard Non-Empty type → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Save Execution Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Sort Jobs Newest First → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and HubSpot aligned by hand for utilities
- Utilities work where "Fetch Changes (Google Sheets)" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Utilities work that only reaches Google Sheets on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and HubSpot in step for utilities, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Google Sheets or HubSpot call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this utilities build
- Every utilities run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Google Sheets
- Fans the same result out to Telegram in the same run, for utilities
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 17 nodes for utilities before wiring Google Sheets

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2 / service account; HubSpot private-app token; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The pipeline is incremental, not full-refresh: it stores a watermark (the last-seen timestamp) and only asks the source for records newer than that, which is what keeps a scheduled re-run cheap instead of re-pulling the entire dataset every time. The tradeoff is that a failed watermark write must be safe to retry — which is exactly why the destination write is an upsert, not a plain insert.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Manually roll the watermark back and re-run — confirm the upsert makes the replay safe (no duplicates).
2. Trigger a reconcile mismatch on purpose and confirm the drift alarm fires.
3. Point the source at a different platform and see how little else in the workflow has to change.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your utilities process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole utilities payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
